title: Migration Symphony: cross-product launch kit and phased sunset orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: deliver a repeatable, cross-functional launch kit for deprecating legacy API surface (v1 variants) while ensuring customer migration to the new runtime-2.0-compatible endpoints with minimal disruption. This ticket coordinates tactical deliverables across Product, Engineering, Design, Docs, DevRel, Support, and Sales for a sequenced, metrics-driven sunset. The kit includes: phased cutover calendar, release notes templates, console banners and in-product migration prompts, SDK warnings and linters, migration guides with example mappings, rollback criteria, and post-migration success playbooks.
acceptance_criteria:
- Public migration guide published in docs with code snippets for Node/Python/Go and example token cost comparisons
- Console banner and in-product migration CTA deployed to 20% of orgs in canary mode
- SDKs (js, py) emit deprecation warnings by default and include automated codemod scripts
- Release notes templates ready and synchronized with engineering PRs and changelogs
- Support runbook and escalation matrix uploaded to internal wiki
- Telemetry dashboards created: migration adoption, API error delta, latency delta, and customer rollback signals
- Cross-team dry run completed with at least two internal product teams and one pilot customer

communication_plan: Phase 0 (Announcement): Targeted email + console banner to pilot customers, internal all-hands summary, and public blog post announcing timeline. Phase 1 (Guidance): Publish migration guide, SDK codemods, and detailed release notes; host two live office hours and record migration walkthrough. Phase 2 (Cutover): Staged console prompts and automated migrations for eligible customers; weekly status updates to stakeholders. Phase 3 (Sunset): Final notice 30/14/7 days before enforced cutover, post-mortem and customer outreach to any blocked orgs.
rollout_timeline:
- Week 0 (Dec 1): Finalize migration guide and release notes template.
- Week 2 (Dec 15): SDK warnings merged; codemod beta published.
- Week 4 (Jan 5): Console banner design implemented; canary to 5% orgs.
- Week 8 (Feb 2): Pilot migrations with 3 customers; gather feedback and fix major regressions.
- Week 12 (Mar 1): Open migration to all customers; start 30/14/7 day notices.
- Week 16 (Mar 29): Enforced cutover date (if acceptance metrics met) or extend by 2 weeks per rollback criteria.
success_metrics: Migration adoption: 70% of active orgs migrated within 8 weeks of open migration
Error rate delta: no more than 2x increase in client-visible 5xxs during migration
Latency impact: median tail latency increase <= 10% for migrated traffic
Support volume: customer tickets related to migration <= 15% week-over-week spike
Regression rate: zero critical correctness regressions in top-10 customer flows
risks:
- Undiscovered SDK incompatibilities causing mass rollbacks
- Console banner/messaging ignored by customers resulting in low adoption
- Telemetry gaps that prevent fast detection of regressions
- Enterprise contracts or regulatory holdouts requiring manual exceptions
- Rollout automation bugs that incorrectly classify eligible customers
notes: Planning assumption: runtime-2.0 will be feature-compatible with v1 request shape for 95% of endpoints; exceptions must be enumerated in the migration guide. Recommended mitigation: provide a 'compatibility shim' library for edge transformations and retain a safety fallback tier for 4 weeks after enforced cutover. PM to run weekly syncs with engineering until sunset is complete. Archive all lessons learned into a post-mortem doc and a reusable kit for future deprecations.
